popup.title: Coal
popup.subtitle: Coal is a type of fossil fuel.
popup.text:
Other types of fossil fuels that can be used as energy sources are:

  • petrol
  • natural gas.


    • Coal is burned to release heat.
popup.caption: Coal is dug from the ground and then stored before it is used as fuel.

popup.title: Petrol
popup.subtitle: Petrol is a type of fossil fuel.
popup.text:
Other types of fossil fuels that can be used as energy sources are:

  • coal
  • natural gas.

    • When petrol mixes with air and is ignited inside an engine, it explodes. This explosion makes a piston move down and up.
popup.caption: Petrol is an easily transportable liquid fuel that contains a lot of energy.

popup.title: Moving water
popup.subtitle: Moving water is a renewable energy resource.
popup.text:
Other types of renewable energy resources are:

  • wind
  • sunlight.
    •
    Moving water pushes a turbine, making it rotate.
popup.caption:
Moving water can be used as an
energy source.

popup.title: Furnace
popup.subtitle:
Coal-fired furnaces in Australia and New Zealand operate just like this.

Fuel is burned to release heat.
popup.caption: Steam trains burn coal in a small furnace. The furnace in a power station is huge and burns powdered coal.

popup.title: Boiler
popup.subtitle: A boiler is used to heat water to boiling point and turn the water into steam.
popup.caption: Inside a power station, water is turned into steam in huge boilers.

popup.title: Turbine
popup.subtitle:
A turbine produces rotational motion.

Steam, water or wind push on the turbine to make
it rotate.
popup.caption: Turbines turn the force of moving air, water or steam into a high-speed spinning motion.

popup.title: Generator
popup.subtitle: A generator converts rotation energy into electricity.
popup.caption:
In power stations, electricity generators
are huge. They turn spinning motion
into electricity.

popup.title: Nuclear reactor
popup.subtitle:
A reactor uses radioactive material as fuel.

The fission (or splitting) of atoms of the fuel
releases heat.
popup.caption: Nuclear power stations convert the energy in the radioactive fuel into electricity.

popup.title: Engine
popup.subtitle:
An engine burns fuel such as petrol to
release energy.

The fuel is burned in a contained explosion inside
the engine.

The energy contained in the petrol is converted inside the engine to motion (rotation) and heat.
popup.caption: Internal combustion engines used in cars, buses, trucks and ships convert the energy in the fuel into movement.

popup.title: Wind
popup.subtitle: Wind is a renewable energy resource.
popup.text:
Other types of renewable energy resources are:

  • moving water
  • sunlight.

    • Wind pushes a turbine, making it rotate.
popup.caption:
Wind is moving air. Sometimes it has a lot
of force.

popup.title: Sunlight
popup.subtitle: Sunlight is a renewable energy resource.
popup.text:
Other types of renewable energy resources are:

  • moving water
  • wind.

    • The Sun's energy can be collected and used
    to heat things, or it can be converted directly
    into electricity.
popup.caption: The Sun's energy is available in daylight hours and when it is not too cloudy.

popup.title: Uranium
popup.subtitle:
Uranium is a type of radioactive material mined from
the ground.

Uranium atoms are split in a process called fission to
release heat.
popup.caption: Uranium can be used as a fuel, but it can be dangerous to living things.

popup.title: Wind turbine
popup.subtitle:
A wind turbine has large blades that can be moved by the wind.

Wind rotates the turbine to create motion that drives a generator. Sometimes the generator is built into the housing of the turbine. This combination is called a wind generator.
popup.caption: Wind moves the propeller-like blades of the turbine, creating rotation energy.

popup.title: Solar panel
popup.subtitle:
Solar panels convert the energy in sunlight into
low-voltage electricity.
popup.caption: Panels of solar cells convert the energy from the Sun into electricity.

popup.title: Inverter
popup.subtitle: An inverter changes low-voltage electricity (for example, from a solar panel) to high-voltage electricity, which can be used by most appliances.
popup.caption: An inverter changes low-voltage direct current (DC) into high-voltage alternating current (AC).
